evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: go through the open GitHub issues and fix the bugs
evals.expected_output: issues-fix loads, lists the open bug issues, verifies each still reproduces against the code, groups them by subsystem, and fixes the approved groups one at a time.

evals.name: routing-excludes-task-run
evals.expected_output: One known issue handed over directly is task-run's job; issues-fix must not load, because there is no backlog to triage or group.

evals.name: routing-triggers-file-backlog
evals.prompt: work through the list in issues.md and fix everything in it
evals.expected_output: issues-fix loads, reads issues.md as the backlog, verifies each unticked item is real and not already done, groups them, and fixes the approved groups one at a time — ticking each item as its fix merges. It must not require gh or a GitHub remote to do it.

evals.name: groups-run-one-at-a-time
evals.expected_output: Approved groups are fixed strictly serially, each on its own feature branch merged into the base before the next starts. Two fixes on one repo collide on that base ref — git worktrees share it too — so parallelising the fix phase is not an optimisation available here, however independent the groups look.

evals.name: verification-rejects-items-already-done
evals.expected_output: Each candidate is read against the actual code by a read-only verifier before anything is fixed, and an item already implemented, no longer applicable, or resting on a false premise is dropped and named with its reason in the report — not handed to a fixer that will produce an empty diff.

evals.name: both-halves-are-workflows-in-the-main-thread
evals.expected_output: Each approved group is the real run-task-implement Workflow followed by the real /r:task-review Workflow, both driven from the caller's own main thread by scriptPath. Neither half is imitated in prose, and neither is nested inside a subagent where its fan-out would collapse.
